title: Swiss Website Budget and Quote Normaliser
note: Spec/data file for the artifact described in ARTIFACT-BRIEF.md. This is structured content only — no HTML/JS is implemented here. This tool never computes, estimates or displays a fabricated CHF total; any total shown is only ever a plain label the reader typed in themselves. No quote (including one labelled 'Weissmann') ever receives special treatment in the logic or the visuals.

categories.label: Page count, defined precisely
categories.description: An exact, named list of pages, not an unbounded "up to X pages".

categories.label: Copywriting responsibility
categories.description: Who delivers the final text: you, the provider, or is this left unstated?

categories.label: Design origin (custom vs. template)
categories.description: A visual identity built specifically for you, or a licensed theme with your colours applied?

categories.label: Language count, stated as a number
categories.description: "Multilingual" is an adjective; a serious quote states how many languages and which ones.

categories.label: Technical SEO & GEO foundation
categories.description: Sitemap, structured data and crawlability named concretely, not the single word "SEO."

categories.label: Analytics setup (GA4 / Search Console)
categories.description: Configured against your actual goals, or an unread tracking snippet.

categories.label: Hosting & maintenance
categories.description: One-time or recurring, and at what ongoing cost.

categories.label: Ownership after handover
categories.description: Do you receive the code and source files, or stay dependent on the provider?

categories.label: Integrations (CRM / booking / payment)
categories.description: Priced into this quote, or the subject of a second quote you have not seen yet?

categories.label: Timeline & dependency on your content
categories.description: What happens to the schedule if your content or approvals arrive late?

categories.label: Post-launch support minimum
categories.description: A defined minimum included, or every hour billed individually?

categories.label: VAT treatment (net or gross)
categories.description: Is the headline figure net or gross of the Swiss standard VAT rate?

comparisonLogic.note: No numeric scoring, no weighting, no invented price. Purely a category-by-category status comparison across entered quotes.
comparisonLogic.activationRule: Comparison view activates only once at least two quotes each have at least one category set to something other than 'not_stated'.

perCategoryRules.condition: all entered quotes have status in [included, excluded] for this category (none not_stated)
perCategoryRules.display: Show each quote's status and note side by side.

perCategoryRules.condition: one or more entered quotes have status == not_stated for this category
perCategoryRules.display: Name exactly which quote(s) are missing this category; add it to their gap list.

perCategoryRules.condition: entered quotes' statuses disagree (e.g. one included, another excluded) for this category
perCategoryRules.display: Highlight as 'Different scope — not the same offer'. This is informative, not an error.

completeness.formula: count of categories with status != not_stated, out of 13, per quote
completeness.rule: Never converted into a percentage bar, star rating, or any quality/price-correlated score.

comparabilityBanner.incomplete: These totals are not yet comparable — {n} categories are still unclear across your quotes.
comparabilityBanner.complete: All categories specified for every quote — the totals below now describe the same scope.
comparabilityBanner.rule: Descriptive only. Never a recommendation of which quote to choose, even when complete.

totalsDisplay.rule: If total_chf is entered for any quote, show all entered totals as a plain, equally-styled label list directly beneath the comparability banner. No ranking, no colour-coding by amount, no 'best value' badge, ever.

noSpecialTreatmentRule: Every quote label (including one the reader names 'Weissmann') is treated identically by all logic and all styling. No quote is ever auto-flagged as recommended, best-value, or otherwise favoured.

gapMessage.template: Before I compare this with another proposal, could you confirm {missingCategoryLabels} so I'm comparing like for like?
gapMessage.allSpecifiedMessage: This quote specifies all thirteen categories — no follow-up needed.

copyButton.label: Copy message
copyButton.fallback: manual-select, no visible error thrown on failure

errorStates.condition: fewer than 2 quotes have any category set
errorStates.behavior: Show only that single quote's own gap list (all 13 categories not yet specified). Prompt: 'Add a second quote to see a side-by-side comparison.'
UI does not offer a fourth slot. Note: 'Compare in groups of up to three quotes at a time for clarity.'

errorStates.condition: a quote has all 13 categories still not_stated
errorStates.behavior: Label it 'Not enough detail to evaluate yet'; exclude it from the per-category comparison table until at least one category is set; suggest sending its full (13-item) gap message to that provider first.
Static HTML lists all 13 categories with plain-language descriptions and the 3 status options in a readable, unfiltered order.

privacyNote: The tool runs fully in the browser. No field asks for a full company name, personal name, email or address — quote labels default to 'Quote A/B/C' and the tool suggests keeping them generic. No data is transmitted or sent to a server.
disclaimerText: This tool does not calculate or estimate a price. It compares what each of your quotes says — and does not say — across thirteen scope categories, so the totals you already have finally describe the same thing. It does not recommend a provider, and it works the same way regardless of who sent the quotes you enter.

primary.label: Request an itemized Weissmann quote in this same scope format

secondary.label: Read the full method behind these thirteen categories
